captions.instagram:
How does a steam press work?

Two thousand watts into a thick metal plate, a strip of two metals that clicks it on and off, and a few drops of water that flash into steam. Take an iron apart in 3D, see why steam unlocks a crease, and meet the laundry's boiler press and the istri-wala's charcoal iron.

→ A steam iron is a thick hot plate, a heating element cast inside it, a thermostat and a tank of water.
→ The laundry's press adds a boiler at a few bar and a table that sucks the steam through the cloth.
→ A crease is long chain molecules bent into a fold and held by hydrogen bonds.
→ Steam slips between the chains, heat lets them slide, and the iron presses them flat. Cooling locks the shape.
→ The thermostat is a strip of two metals: it curls as it warms and clicks the element off and on.

youtubeLong.description:
Two thousand watts into a thick metal plate, a strip of two metals that clicks it on and off, and a few drops of water that flash into steam. Take an iron apart in 3D, see why steam unlocks a crease, and meet the laundry's boiler press and the istri-wala's charcoal iron.

▶ Play with the interactive version: https://glassbox.how/e/steampressclear/
⌘ Source code (MIT): https://github.com/bdeeps/steampressclear

In this video:
• A hot plate, a thermostat and some water. A steam iron is a thick aluminium or steel soleplate with a heating element cast inside it, a bimetal thermostat under the dial, and a water tank whose drip valve lets drops fall into a steam chamber on the hot plate.
• Steam unlocks the crease. Cotton and wool chains are held in a fold by hydrogen bonds.
• The heat sums. The soleplate stores about 620 J per degree, so 2,000 W brings it to 200 °C in about a minute.
• The laundry's boiler press. A small boiler at 4 bar holds water at about 152 °C.
• The istri-wala's charcoal iron. Five kilograms of cast iron store about 2,300 J per degree, so the istri-wala's box iron stays hot between loads of charcoal; blowing on the coals gives them more air and more heat.
• Safe and lasting. A gram of steam condensing on skin gives about ten times the heat of a gram of boiling water.
